subject: making observers using a loop (for or lapply)

messages.author: f6dea426c8b7a030
messages.subject: making observers using a loop (for or lapply)
parts:
Just a little solution in case anyone finds it useful.
It took me a while to figure this out.

If you want to put a set of observe() objects in your shiny server session
using a for() or lapply(), 
the call to observe() needs to assign the observer to a variable name.
Otherwise, only the last value takes hold.

Thus this example works fine,
but if you leave out the assign statement,
only observer #7 is registered in the server:

  obs = function(number)
    assign("obs" %&% number,
           observe({
             newValue <- input[["stepStatus" %&% number]]
             catn("Toggling stepStatus" %&% number %&% " = " %&% newValue)
             isolate({ # necessary, or else crash!
               rValues$stepsTable[number, "Done?"] = newValue
               catn("New value in stepsTable: ",
                    rValues$stepsTable[number, "Done?"] )
             })
           }
           )
    )
  lapply(1:7, obs)

messages.subject: Re: making observers using a loop (for or lapply)
parts:
I was asked for more details, so here:

I have a set of 7 radio button sets as part of seven sections.

In ui.R, I place calls to sectionHeader(), defined as:
sectionHeader = function(number) {
  list(hr(),
       h2(paste0('(', number, ') ',
                 stepsTableInitial[number, "Stepping stone"])),
       h3("Question " %&% number, ": ",
          stepsTableInitial[number, "Question"]),
  span(
   radioButtons("stepStatus" %&% number,
                 label="Is this step done?", choices=c("Not yet", "Done"))
  )
}

The radioButton ID’s are stepStatus1 … stepStatus7.
The observers created in server.R allow the interface to respond to radioButton clicks:
update values in a tableOutput, enable or disable a button, ...

But, the point is that without the “assign” wrapper, 
    assign("obs" %&% number,...)
only the last radioButton set is observed.

I hope this helps!

messages.subject: Re: making observers using a loop (for or lapply)
parts:
Yup, I just tried it again— with lapply.

After commenting out the assign(),
on startup I get 
Toggling stepStatus7 = Not yet 
New value in stepsTable:  Not yet 
Toggling stepStatus7 = Not yet 
New value in stepsTable:  Not yet 
Toggling stepStatus7 = Not yet 
New value in stepsTable:  Not yet 
Toggling stepStatus7 = Not yet 
New value in stepsTable:  Not yet 
Toggling stepStatus7 = Not yet 
New value in stepsTable:  Not yet 
Toggling stepStatus7 = Not yet 
New value in stepsTable:  Not yet 
Toggling stepStatus7 = Not yet 
New value in stepsTable:  Not yet 
and then only the 7th radio set responds to use clicks.
Restoring the assign() call, all is well. On startup:
 Toggling stepStatus1 = Not yet 
New value in stepsTable:  Not yet 
Toggling stepStatus2 = Not yet 
New value in stepsTable:  Not yet 
Toggling stepStatus3 = Not yet 
New value in stepsTable:  Not yet 
Toggling stepStatus4 = Not yet 
New value in stepsTable:  Not yet 
Toggling stepStatus5 = Not yet 
New value in stepsTable:  Not yet 
Toggling stepStatus6 = Not yet 
New value in stepsTable:  Not yet 
Toggling stepStatus7 = Not yet 
and all the radio sets work. for example, clicking the first one gives
Toggling stepStatus1 = Done 
New value in stepsTable:  Done 
I was unsurprised that the for loop failed,
but very surprised that the lapply failed
(until wrapping in assign()).

messages.author: f6dea426c8b7a030
messages.subject: Re: making observers using a loop (for or lapply)
parts:
Also, I tried moving the “assign” from inside the iterated function 
to the lapply statement.
That doesn’t work either.

It’s a moot point, since we have the solution— put the “assign” into the obs() function--
but still, it’s mighty curious!

Inspecting the result of the lapply,
it’s a list of observers of course,
but apparently somehow the last value of the index “number”
migrates into all the observers,
so they all observe the 7th radio button set.

Also curious: right after the assign() (in the function obs(), in the successful version),
neither find() nor getAnywhere() can find the observe object that was 
just assigned.

Again, this is all moot, but puzzling.
